message:
When attempting to unshare a node from the primary namespace, return
errorMachineNotShared, not errorSameNamespace. Add test for same.

cli changes for the `nodes` subcommand:

* when listing nodes, a namespace is now optional, when it is not
  provided, all nodes are shown
* when deleting, and sharing a node, remove the `namespace` flag, it was
  superfluous and unused
* when unsharing a node, specify the namespace as an argument not a
  flag, making the UX the same as for sharing.

Also refactor the share/unshare code to reuse the shared bits.

body: For the sharing/unsharing cli syntax, we now have 2 arguments and order matters. The alternative approach would be to go for named flags, which is more verbose but it would mean they could be supplied in any order. Do you have a preference?

Looks good, I agree with this, would be interested to hear @juanfont.

and here some opinions of these two:

> For the sharing/unsharing cli syntax, we now have 2 arguments and order matters. The alternative approach would be to go for named flags, which is more verbose but it would mean they could be supplied in any order. Do you have a preference?

I am a bit mixed, in general, I am a fan of explicit keywords and things that describe what value I am entering, so more than one positional is a bit iffy to me. But for the current context I think it might be ok.

(I just prefer coming back to a script and seeing --that-arugmument abc --that-other def)

I don't have a strong opinion on this, but I tend to agree with @kradalby on making the CLI as verbose as possible & reasonable. At the end of the day, for automation/faster-than-CLI purposes we will be needing reworking headscale to include a control API of its own.

Having said that, I love this commit!

message: Make the cli help a little more explicit for the nodes subcommand.

Move the namespace argument back to a flag for the share and unshare
commands.

body:
All right so with that last push, the syntax for share/unshare now lines up with the one for "register": the namespace is a required flag, not a positional argument. That means we now have: 
headscale nodes delete ID
headscale nodes list (-n optional)
headscale nodes register machineID -n namespace
headscale nodes share ID -n namespace
headscale nodes unshare ID -n namespace
Confusingly, `machineID` is not the ID field of a node entry, but a long random-ish string. We could further streamline the cli UX to: 
headscale nodes delete -i ID
headscale nodes list (-n optional)
headscale nodes register -m machineID -n namespace
headscale nodes share -i ID -n namespace
headscale nodes unshare -i ID -n namespace
wdyt @juanfont @kradalby ?

> We could further streamline the cli UX to:
> 
> headscale nodes delete -i ID
> headscale nodes list (-n optional)
> headscale nodes register -m machineID -n namespace
> headscale nodes share -i ID -n namespace
> headscale nodes unshare -i ID -n namespace
> wdyt @juanfont @kradalby ?

I think I like this, to me an important factor is the long flag, as that what I use in script so they are "self documenting", but Im all for making them easy to type otherwise. 

So `-i` -> `--identifier` ?
and `-n` -> `--namespace`

(This is mostly for the record, I see that it is implemented that way)

I think making things explicit is very important and this will allow us to use the long flag in documentation so it _might_ be easier to understand and have lower cognitive load for new (and old) users.
